per_article_summaries: Guenther Steiner has criticised Aston Martin's performance at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix. The former Haas Formula 1 team principal branded the Silverstone outfit's current campaign "not acceptable" Steiner rejected the idea that team owner Lawrence Stroll lacked commitment.

Williams team principal James Vowles is confident of keeping Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz for next season. Vowles says that both drivers have bought into the project and that they "want their future" to be at Williams. Vowles added that the drivers would be "foolish" not to consider their options.

Martin Brundle has branded the handling of the Monaco Grand Prix pitlane penalties and Pierre Gasly's reinstated podium "a mess with no easy solution" Several drivers were handed penalties during the Monaco Grand Prix for speeding in the pitlane. While the majority of those drivers served the penalties during the race, Gasly, who finished third on the road, had the time added after the chequered flag and lost the podium as a result.

Lewis Hamilton won the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix for Ferrari. Juan Pablo Montoya has likened the seven-time champion's mentality to that of Fernando Alonso. Hamilton ended a victory drought stretching back to the 2024 Belgian Grand Prix, pulling off a three-stop strategy that reinvigorated his 2026 title campaign.

Mercedes has identified an issue with its battery that is at the heart of its recent F1 race retirements which have cost both George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. The team has pinpointed the issue to its power unit’s battery and a permanent fix is being worked on. Mercedes hasn't given a timeline on when the ‘proper cure’ will be ready.

Ferrari is waiting for official approval from the FIA before introducing its upgraded Formula 1 engine, provisionally as early as the Austrian Grand Prix. The updated power unit pushes the concept of its steel-alloy cylinder head even further. Using a steel alloy rather than aluminium for the cylinder head allows combustion chamber temperatures to be significantly higher.

1997 Formula 1 champion Jacques Villeneuve has argued that Ferrari must throw its full weight behind Lewis Hamilton if the Maranello outfit is to have any chance of winning the 2026 championship. The seven-time champion secured his maiden grand prix victory as a Ferrari driver in Barcelona, which ended his win drought.

Guenther Steiner has labelled the FIA's decision to reinstate Pierre Gasly's Monaco Grand Prix podium a "debacle" Steiner warned that the ruling has opened a massive can of worms for Formula 1's regulatory consistency. The former Haas team principal gave a characteristically blunt assessment of the post-race decision.

Lewis Hamilton took his first win for Ferrari at the 31st time of asking. Only three drivers have required even more time to win for the Scuderia. Eddie Irvine, Jean Alesi and Carlos Sainz were the longest to break their duck.

Oliver Bearman admits he entered Australian Grand Prix with the "wrong mindset" The British driver suffered a crash during the first practice session at Albert Park. Bearman finished the race from the pitlane and finished in 14th place. He finished his rookie season 13th in the drivers' championship with 41 points.

Daniel Ricciardo has opened up about his first visit to the Indianapolis 500. The eight-time grand prix winner has embraced a different lifestyle since leaving F1. Ricciardo is enjoying the perks of being a Ford Racing ambassador. The Australian is focusing on his clothing brand, Enchanté.

Claire Williams believes that only a select few drivers in Formula 1 history have the personality type to transform a team. Williams reflected on Lewis Hamilton's second season at Ferrari. The seven-time champion recently secured a landmark 106th career victory.

Robert Kubica won the Le Mans 24 Hours in 2025 with AF Corse Ferrari. The Polish driver had signed a contract with Ferrari for the 2012 season. But the deal fell through because of a rallying accident in 2011. Kubica spent a year and a half away from racing, and it took six years to return.

Lewis Hamilton spotted at the wheel of Ferrari's legendary three-seater. The car was designed by Rory Byrne in 2003 and was based on the F2002. It's powered by a 3.0-litre, 10-cylinder engine that delivers over 800 horsepower. The seven-time champion is currently second in the drivers' championship.
